Bring a little of the Italian coast into your bathroom with this gorgeous set of three watercolour-style art prints inspired by the Amalfi Coast. Each print has a loose, painterly quality — soft whites and muted blues washed through with warm terracotta, sage green, dusty pink and earthy neutrals — and together they tell a story of long, lazy lunches by the sea. If you've ever dreamed of a bathroom that feels like a boutique hotel on the Mediterranean, this set of three is the easiest way to get there without leaving home.

The three prints work beautifully as a trio. The left print shows a coastal café table laid with seafood, wine and olives, with sailboats drifting across a pale blue bay in the background. The centre print depicts a charming white-rendered building flanked by tall palm trees — with the handwritten phrase Sotto il sole d'Amalfi (Under the Amalfi sun) inscribed beneath it in delicate script. The right print returns to a sun-drenched terrace scene: a round café table set with a small feast of antipasti, fresh flowers and drinks, with the whitewashed hillside town and shimmering blue sea stretching out behind. The palette is calm and cohesive — soft blue, warm white, touches of coral and green — making all three prints feel like they belong together without being overly matchy.

How to Style decor for bathroom with This Coastal Set

I'd hang all three in a row at the same height, with an even gap between each print — somewhere around 5–8 cm works nicely and keeps the set feeling intentional rather than random. If your bathroom has a longer wall above the bath or behind the sink, this trio slots in perfectly. The soft blue and white tones play really well with brushed chrome or matt white fixtures, and if you've got any natural wood shelving or rattan accessories in there, the warm terracotta and earthy tones in the prints will pick those up beautifully. For a full Mediterranean mood, pair with white fluffy towels, a terracotta pot or two, and maybe a trailing plant on a shelf.

Not just for bathrooms, though — this set looks wonderful in a kitchen-diner, hallway or even a sitting room. Anywhere you want a little warmth and a holiday feeling, really. For more coastal and Mediterranean wall art ideas, have a browse through our Coastal Wall Art collection — there are some lovely companions to this set in there.

Choosing the Right Size and Finish for Your Space

Before you pick a size, it's worth holding a piece of paper up to your wall (or using painter's tape) to mark out how much space you actually have. For a bathroom, a smaller or medium size per print often works better than going very large — you want the set to feel curated, not cramped. That said, if you have a generous wall above a freestanding bath, don't be shy about going bigger; the detail in these illustrations really rewards a closer look at a larger size.

For finish, I'd genuinely recommend the canvas-wrapped option if your bathroom gets steamy. Canvas is moisture-resistant in a way that paper prints simply aren't, so it holds up much better in a damp, high-moisture environment — it's the practical choice as well as a beautiful one. If your bathroom is well-ventilated or you're planning to hang these in another room, the Luster art paper gives a lovely soft sheen, while Museum quality paper is the one for really rich, true-to-life colour depth.

aiItems.content:
What is decor for bathroom?

Bathroom decor refers to the decorative items you add to a bathroom to give it personality, warmth and style — and wall art prints are one of the most effective ways to do that. A well-chosen set of prints can make a plain bathroom feel like a considered, designed space rather than a purely functional room. In a coastal or Mediterranean style, soft blue and white tones with painted or illustrative artwork are especially popular, as they create a calm, airy feel that suits the relaxing nature of a bathroom. Choosing prints that are moisture-aware — such as canvas-wrapped options — means your decor stays looking great even in a steamy environment.

How to Hang Decor for Bathroom: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Choose your wall: Pick a wall with enough clear space for all three prints side by side — above the bath, behind the loo or beside the sink are all great spots. Avoid walls directly above a shower where steam and splashes are most intense.

2. Decide on your layout: For a set of three, a straight horizontal row at eye level is the most timeless arrangement. Mark the centre point of your wall and work outward, leaving an equal gap (around 5–8 cm) between each print.

3. Use a spirit level: Even a small tilt is noticeable with three prints in a row. A small spirit level or a spirit-level app on your phone will save you a lot of re-hanging.

4. Pick the right hanging method: In a bathroom, damage-free adhesive picture strips work well on tiled or painted walls and avoid the need for drilling. For heavier framed options, a single picture hook into a wall stud is the most secure.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three are up, step back to check the spacing and alignment before you commit. It's much easier to make small adjustments now than after everything is fully secured.

Which Option Is Right for Your Bathroom? Comparing Print Formats

Unframed Print (Luster or Museum paper) — The most affordable option; you choose your own frame. Best for well-ventilated bathrooms or other rooms. Luster paper gives a soft, semi-gloss finish; Museum quality paper delivers the richest, deepest colour reproduction.

Framed Print (Luster or Museum paper) — Arrives ready to hang straight out of the box — no frame-hunting needed. A great choice if you want a polished, finished look immediately. Best suited to bathrooms with good ventilation rather than very high moisture.

Wrapped Canvas — The best choice for damp, steamy bathrooms. Canvas is moisture-resistant, making it far more durable in high-humidity environments than paper prints. Also arrives ready to hang, with the print wrapped neatly around a solid frame — no additional framing required. A beautiful, gallery-style finish.

aiItems.content:
What is a bathroom painting?

A bathroom painting is a piece of wall art — typically a print, canvas, or original artwork — chosen specifically to be displayed in a bathroom, restroom, or WC. Because bathrooms tend to be smaller, more functional spaces, bathroom paintings are a simple and affordable way to add personality, colour, and a decorative focal point without a full redecoration. Popular styles include coastal, botanical, abstract, and typographic designs, and they work in everything from compact cloakrooms to large family bathrooms. For damp or steamy bathrooms, a moisture-resistant option such as a wrapped canvas print is usually the most practical choice.

How to Hang a Bathroom Painting Set of 3

1. Measure your wall first: Use a tape measure to find the total width of the wall or the section you want to fill. Aim for the combined width of all three prints to cover around two-thirds of that space — this keeps things balanced and avoids the prints looking too small or too cramped.

2. Mark the centre point: Find the centre of your wall section and use a pencil to mark it lightly. Hang the middle print centred on this mark, then work outwards to position the left and right prints with an equal gap between each one — 5 to 8 cm is a good starting point.

3. Hang at eye level: The centre of each print should sit at roughly eye level, which for most people is around 145–150 cm from the floor. In a bathroom where you spend time seated (near a toilet or bath), you can go slightly lower so the art is comfortable to look at from that position.

4. Use a spirit level: Even small differences in height are very noticeable with a set of three. A small spirit level or a free spirit-level app on your phone takes seconds and saves a lot of frustration.

5. Consider moisture: In a steamy bathroom, choose the canvas-wrapped option for your prints — it's moisture-resistant and will last far longer than a paper print in a high-humidity environment.

Choosing Your Bathroom Painting Format: Which Option Is Right for You?

Unframed Print — Luster or Museum quality art paper. Perfect if you already have a frame you love or want to frame it yourself. You receive the print only — ready to put in your own frame.

Framed Print — Luster or Museum quality art paper, presented in a frame. Arrives ready to hang straight away — no extra shopping needed. A great all-round choice for well-ventilated bathrooms.

Wrapped Canvas — Printed on canvas and stretched over a wooden frame. No glass, no frame needed — arrives completely ready to hang. The best choice for bathrooms, restrooms, and any damp or high-moisture room, as canvas is naturally moisture-resistant and holds up far better over time.

Paper quality: Luster — A slight sheen that makes colours pop. Versatile, beautiful finish suitable for most interiors.

Paper quality: Museum — A premium matte finish with exceptional colour depth. Ideal if you want the look and feel of a fine-art print.

aiItems.content:
What is wall art greenery?

Wall art greenery refers to art prints, canvases or framed pieces that feature botanical subjects — leaves, branches, plants or foliage — bringing a sense of nature and calm into your home. The style ranges from loose watercolour botanicals and abstract leaf compositions to more detailed illustrative prints, and it sits comfortably in farmhouse, Scandi, boho and modern-classic interiors alike. It is one of the core expressions of biophilic design, which is all about weaving natural shapes, colours and textures into your living spaces to create a more relaxed and restorative environment. Wall art greenery works particularly well in bathrooms, living rooms, hallways and bedrooms, where the earthy greens and botanical forms introduce a quiet, organic energy without requiring you to maintain a single real plant.

How to Hang and Style Wall Art Greenery in Your Home

1. Choose your wall and measure up: Pick a wall with enough room for all three prints side by side. Measure the wall width and aim for the combined print width to fill roughly two-thirds of it — this creates a balanced, intentional look rather than prints that look lost or crowded.

2. Mark your hanging points at eye level: Eye level is typically around 145–150 cm from the floor to the centre of the print. Use a pencil and a spirit level to mark where each print will sit, keeping an even gap of 5–8 cm between them for a clean, gallery-style arrangement.

3. Match your wall colour to the palette: The greens and ochre tones in botanical greenery art look their best against warm white, off-white, sage or stone walls. Hold a paint swatch next to the print image before you commit — it takes seconds and saves regrets.

4. Choose the right format for the room: For bathrooms or any high-moisture space, opt for the wrapped canvas format as it handles damp conditions far better than paper prints. For living rooms, bedrooms and hallways, Luster or Museum quality paper prints both look excellent.

5. Style with natural accessories: Once hung, bring the look together with a few natural-material accessories nearby — a wooden shelf, a woven basket, a trailing pothos or some dried pampas grass. Botanical wall art and real plants genuinely complement one another beautifully.

Unframed, Framed or Wrapped Canvas — Which Option is Right for You?

Arrives ready to hang — Unframed print: No (you supply your own frame). Framed print: Yes, ready to hang straight away. Wrapped canvas: Yes, ready to hang straight away.

Paper / surface choice — Unframed print: Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Framed print: Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Wrapped canvas: Canvas wrap (no paper option).

Framing flexibility — Unframed print: Full flexibility — you choose your own frame, mount and style. Framed print: Comes framed, no extra sourcing needed. Wrapped canvas: No frame needed — the canvas wraps around a wooden stretcher bar.

Ideal for — Unframed print: Those who already have a frame or want to match existing decor exactly. Framed print: Anyone who wants a polished, complete look with no extra effort. Wrapped canvas: Bathrooms, laundry rooms and anyone who loves a contemporary, frameless gallery feel.
